sources.entry: hyperopt - Distributed asynchronous hyperparameter optimization with Tree-structured Parzen Estimators.

summary.one_liner: Hyperopt is a Python library for serial and parallel hyperparameter optimization over search spaces that can include real-valued, discrete, and conditional dimensions.
summary.what_it_does: Provides fmin() to minimize an objective function over a search space defined with hp.* primitives (choice, uniform, lognormal, and others). It implements random search, Tree of Parzen Estimators (TPE), and Adaptive TPE. Search spaces can be conditional, so different branches of the space can contain different parameters. Optimization can run serially or in parallel through Apache Spark or MongoDB. The space_eval() helper maps the best result back to the actual parameter values. Installation is via PyPI, with optional extras named SparkTrials, MongoTrials, and ATPE.
use_cases: searching conditional or nested parameter spaces
running hyperparameter search in parallel on Spark
distributing trials across workers with MongoDB
how_to_run: Define an objective function and a search space using hp.* functions
space_eval(space, best) to recover the parameter values
notable: Tree of Parzen Estimators (TPE) and Adaptive TPE optimizers
Handles conditional and awkward search spaces with mixed real, discrete, and nested dimensions
Parallel trials via Apache Spark or MongoDB
Ships with a documented contributing workflow including nox multi-version test runs
caveats: README says Gaussian-process and regression-tree Bayesian optimizers are designed for but not currently implemented
Parallel execution requires setting up Spark or MongoDB; the extras are optional
Documentation is partly still hosted on the project wiki
